newsitem.title: QATAR: QATAR AIRWAYS TO DOUBLE CAPITAL, LEASE NEW PLANES-.
newsitem.headline: QATAR AIRWAYS TO DOUBLE CAPITAL, LEASE NEW PLANES-.

text.p: Privately owned Qatar Airways said on Monday it would "double" its $50 million capital, lease two new aircraft and introduce a new coat of paint to take it forward into the next century.
The airline's newly-appointed chief executive officer Akbar al-Baker said these decisions were taken at a board meeting on January 31.

He has also brought in a number of airline executives to strengthen the management team and improved schedules on routes since he took over in October from Sheikh Hamad bin Ali bin Jaber al-Thani, who was suddenly sacked.
Last week, the government allowed the airline to offer more shares to Qatari individuals and institutions. The company is owned by some influential families, a bank and an insurance company.

Baker told reporters the airline would lease two Airbus A300 aircraft from Australian leasing firm Ansett Worldwide for five years at an annual cost of $18 million. The wide-bodied jet can take 238 passengers.
The airline had earlier decided to buy two new wide-bodied planes on credit and invited bids, along with financing proposals, from manufacturers.
"This decision is suspended for the time being", said another airline official.
But he said the company "is still going ahead with the plan to buy a Boeing 727 to meet the need for medium and short-haul" aircraft.

By mid-May, the airline would launch steps to polish its image by introducing new aircraft livery and uniforms at a cost of $2.5 million, Baker. The short-haul boeing fleet is being refitted to enhance passenger comfort.

New schedules were recently introduced, including twice-daily direct services on intra-Gulf routes from Doha to Dubai and Abu Dhabi. There is an increase in frequency from Doha to Cairo and a new thrice-weekly service between Doha and Trivandrum from February 18.
